subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should the cron ghost-run mitigation land as a default-on persisted protocol/UI warning with a configurable threshold, or should it be narrowed to a log-only/operator diagnostic before merge?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the visible fix shape affects config defaults, generated protocol clients, run history, and operator UX, which requires maintainer intent rather than another automatic fix lane.

options.title: Refresh linked PR and settle the warning surface
options.body: Resolve conflicts in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72677, remove unrelated churn if still present, and accept the chosen config/protocol/UI warning shape with exact-head proof.

options.title: Replace with a narrower diagnostic
options.body: Close or pause the broad branch and land a smaller log-only or cron-runs-only warning if maintainers do not want a new config/protocol surface.

options.title: Defer the mitigation
options.body: Leave the current behavior documented as a known limitation only if maintainers decide a threshold-based ghost-run detector is too noisy or misleading.

recommendation.title: Refresh linked PR and settle the warning surface
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72677, remove unrelated churn if still present, and accept the chosen config/protocol/UI warning shape with exact-head proof.
